Hi Samir —

Great questions. I'm looping in Evelyn (security) and Aditya (deployments) to provide the exact control-plane requirements and a recommended hardened configuration. High-level answers below to unblock your SOC review while we produce a detailed artifact:

- Domains/endpoints: Allow outbound HTTPS (443) to *.control.redwood-inference.internal and telemetry.redwood-inference.com. We also use a signed object store for model downloads at models.blob.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS only).
- IP ranges: We recommend FQDN-based allowlisting for stability; however customers with strict IP policies can use the CIDR ranges we provide in the attached PDF. The ranges are updated quarterly.
- Ports: 443 outbound for API/control/metrics and 80 only for redirect to 443 during initial bootstrap (can be blocked after). No other persistent outbound ports required.
- Inbound: Redwood will not initiate inbound connections to your control plane. All coordination is initiated from your side.
- TLS & certs: TLS 1.2+ with SNI is required. We sign our TLS certificates with public CAs; mutual TLS is optional — we support mTLS with client certs for higher assurance (see attachment).
- SSH: No evergreen SSH access required. Support sessions (debug) can be performed via a temporary support tunnel initiated by you and audited; we do not keep persistent SSH keys.

Action items: Evelyn will send a hardened checklist and explicit CIDR list (if requested). Aditya will confirm the model download size/timeouts for NAT/egress planning.

Sean

Hi Samir and team —

Attaching a concise hardened egress policy for the on‑prem private deployment. Summary and clarifications below to help the SOC packet:

Policy summary (recommended minimum):
- Outbound only: block all outbound traffic by default, permit only whitelisted FQDNs over TLS 1.2+ on port 443.
- Allowlist preference: prefer FQDN allowlisting with HTTPS; where policy requires IPs, use the quarterly CIDR bundles we publish.
- NAT: Use a set of static SNAT IPs for the control plane to make outbound requests (we'll consume those in our allowlist). If your environment uses ephemeral NAT IPs, plan for automated updates to your firewall.
- DNS: Permit DNS lookups to a controlled resolver (we recommend restricting to your recursive resolvers). Avoid allowing arbitrary external DNS (mitigates exfil). Optionally use DNS over TLS/HTTPS to the resolver.
- Model downloads: /models/* endpoints served via CDN — expect short-lived signed URLs. Large model pulls may use multiple connections; please permit connection concurrency for downloads (heuristic: allow up to 8 concurrent HTTPS connections per host during initial cache warm).
- Heartbeat & telemetry: outbound pings to telemetry.redwood-inference.com every 60s (configurable). Telemetry payloads are batched — disable if you cannot permit telemetry, but note limited diagnostics.
- Support & updates: package updates and health checks are pull-based from your side; no inbound firewall exceptions required. For escalated debug we request a short-lived support tunnel (we provide step-by-step scripts).
- SSH & RDP: blocked by default. If your process requires remote debug, create an ephemeral bastion with recorded session logs and add short-lived rule for our support CIDRs.

Operational notes for SOC packet:
- We sign payloads and model manifests (SHA256 + signature) so you can validate integrity.
- We support client certs for mutual TLS if you need stronger authentication — recommend this for FedRAMP-equivalent workloads.
- If you require static IPs: request CIDR package; we'll provide a set of /24 blocks to minimize churn.

Attached: hardened-egress-checklist.docx (outline of ACL rules & sample firewall entries). If you want, Aditya and I can run a short workshop with your firewall team to translate the checklist into Palo Alto/Check Point rules.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Hey Samir —

Quick technical addendum to Evelyn's guidance with concrete config snippets you can drop into your NAT/firewall team ticket. We've kept this intentionally conservative.

- FQDN allowlist (recommended):
  - control.redwood-inference.internal (API + control plane)
  - telemetry.redwood-inference.com (metrics & heartbeats)
  - models.blob.redwood-inference.com (model artifacts)
  - updates.redwood-inference.com (package metadata)

- If you must use IPs (example CIDRs — please use our attached PDF for authoritative list):
  - 203.0.113.0/24 (control cluster A, example)
  - 198.51.100.0/24 (control cluster B, example)
  - 192.0.2.0/24 (CDN/model downloads, example)
- Ports: TCP/443 (required), TCP/80 (temporary bootstrap only)
- Timeouts: allow 90s idle for download connections; tune NAT timeouts to 120s to avoid premature termination of long downloads.
- Concurrency: allow 6–8 concurrent TLS sessions per VM during cache fill; afterwards steady-state uses 1–2 sessions.

Sample firewall rule (Palo Alto style description):
- Source: private-subnet-xxx
- Destination: FQDN control.redwood-inference.internal (or CIDR 203.0.113.0/24)
- Application/service: ssl
- Action: allow (log at session end)
- Security profile: antivirus + outbound URL filtering restricted to category 'software-distribution'

If you want the exact CIDR bundle we will add you to our quarterly distribution list and provide a signed manifest with a timestamp so your change control can validate. Happy to jump on a short call with your firewall lead — propose Mon 15 Jun at 10am PT.
